- Reverse-charge wording: "VAT to be accounted for by the recipient under Article 194 of Council Directive 2006/112/EC"
- Invoice net of VAT (0% billed)
- Reference to PO #4523

I’ve attached the PO and the current invoice. Please let me know if you need additional evidence (VAT cert, company registration).

We’re trying to close payment this week — can you expedite the reissue?

Marissa / Ben — forwarding an urgent ask from Grace Labs. They say the invoice was issued to the wrong entity and want reverse-charge. They included a VAT ID in the email (IE3456789V) but I ran a quick checksum and it failed in our manual check. Before I reissue anything I need confirmation on two points:

1) Can Revenue Ops confirm whether Grace Labs qualifies for reverse-charge under our rules (EU B2B, goods/services location)?
2) Can Billing run a VAT ID batch validation (do we have earlier validations for this account?) and confirm the correct billing entity mapping (US parent vs EU subsidiary)?

If the VAT ID is not valid, we should not reissue as RC — we need to send an amended invoice or advise on withholding. Also want to avoid creating multiple invoice numbers unnecessarily — happiest path is to cancel INV-20251110 and issue INV-20251110-RC net of VAT with the recommended wording.

Can you take point and loop in Collections if this holds up payment? Grace asked for a same-week turnaround.

Hannah — I pulled the account history and ran our VAT batch checks. Summary below and attached is the validation export.

Quick findings:
- VAT ID IE3456789V: format looks like an optional prefix glitch. The ID in their header doesn't pass checksum in VIES but a server-side script flagged a match to a historical record where the trailing digit differs (likely transcription).
- Grace Labs on file: two legal entities — Grace Labs, Inc. (US) and Grace Labs EU Ltd (IE). The billing relationship on the original contract is to the US entity; however the PO and subsequent emails are requesting the EU entity.

Recommended next steps (in order):
1) Request Grace Labs to upload the VAT certificate (scanner/clearscan) — accept before RC reissue. (quickest proof)
2) If they confirm the EU billing entity plus valid VAT cert, cancel INV-20251110 and issue INV-20251110-RC (net) to Grace Labs EU Ltd with reverse-charge wording. Reference PO #4523 and include both entity names on the invoice header for our audit trail.
3) If VAT ID cannot be validated in VIES, route to Collections for a short payment hold and request remediation — do not issue RC.
4) Log the validation result in HubSpot and attach to the invoice record (HubSpot:HS-72345).

I’ve attached: vat_validation_report_20251121.csv and a screenshot of the VIES lookup (validation_vat_gracelabs.png). I can produce the reissued invoice template (INV-20251110-GL-RC.pdf) ready for your sign-off; however we need affirmative VAT cert or a clear, signed statement from their procurement confirming EU entity.

If you want I can also call Accounts Payable at Grace Labs — their PO indicates a fast-track approval window.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Revenue Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Tom — thanks for the quick note and for the PO. I’m copying Revenue Ops (Marissa) and Collections (Ben) to speed this. Two quick asks so we can reissue the invoice as reverse-charge the same day:

1) Please upload a scanned VAT certificate for Grace Labs EU Ltd (IE3456789V) or confirm the exact VAT number if there was a transcription error. We ran a VIES check and it returned no match; often a missing/extra digit causes that.
2) Confirm the billing entity that should appear on the invoice header: Grace Labs EU Ltd (preferred) OR Grace Labs, Inc (US) — if it’s the EU entity, we will cancel the original invoice and issue INV-20251110-RC net of VAT.

Attached is a draft reissued invoice (INV-20251110-GL-RC.pdf). If you confirm the VAT cert and entity we’ll finalize and send the reissued PDF and updated accounting record.

If for any reason you can’t provide the VAT certificate by EOD, Ben will advise next steps for payment hold.

Best,
